Auger (2016) DBH–height model for 27 Québec tree species

Source: R/hd_auger2016.R
hd_auger2016.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level height–diameter relationship of Auger (2016; Note de recherche forestière no 146) for 27 commercial tree species of Québec. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), plot merchantable basal area and, depending on the species, the tree's relative DBH, climate normals, altitude and Québec ecological classification codes.

Usage

hd_auger2016(
  DBH,
  species,
  BA,
  QMD = NULL,
  SDOM = NULL,
  MP = NULL,
  VP = NULL,
  TMOY = NULL,
  PTOT = NULL,
  altitude = NULL,
  disturbance = NULL
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.MAR"; compact "PICEMAR" is accepted). Supported: ABIE.BAL, ACER.RUB, ACER.SAC, ACER.SAH, BETU.ALL, BETU.PAP, BETU.POP, FAGU.GRA, FRAX.AME, FRAX.NIG, LARI.LAR, OSTR.VIR, PICE.GLA, PICE.MAR, PICE.RUB, PINU.BAN, PINU.RES, PINU.STR, POPU.BAL, POPU.GRA, POPU.TRE, PRUN.SER, QUER.RUB, THUJ.OCC, TILI.AME, TSUG.CAN, ULMU.AME.

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Merchantable basal area of the plot (m²/ha; source "ST", « surface terrière marchande dans la placette », trees with DBH > 9 cm, all species). Must be >= 0. Required for all species.

QMD

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Quadratic mean DBH (cm) of the plot's merchantable trees. Used to compute the relative DBH (RDHP = DBH / QMD). Must be > 0. Required for 21 species.

SDOM

Optional character vector. Plot level. Bioclimatic subdomain (Saucier et al. 1998): "1", "2est", "2ouest", "3est", "3ouest", "4est", "4ouest", "5est", "5ouest", "6est", "6ouest". Required for 11 species.

MP

Optional character or integer vector. Plot level. Physical environment class (« milieu physique », MRN 2013), 0 to 9. Required for 10 species.

VP

Optional character vector. Plot level. Potential vegetation code (e.g. "RS2", "FE3"; three characters). Required for 15 species.

TMOY

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Mean annual temperature, 1981–2010 normal (°C). Required for 7 species.

PTOT

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Total annual precipitation, 1981–2010 normal (mm). Must be >= 0. Required for 10 species.

altitude

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Altitude (m). Required for 4 species.

disturbance

Optional character vector. Plot level. Occurrence of a light disturbance (« perturbation légère »): "anthropique" ("anthropogenic"), "naturelle" ("natural") or "aucune" ("none"). Required for 5 species.

Value

A tibble with column height (m).

Details

Model form (equation 1, p. 4): $$h = 1.3 + A \ln(DBH + 1) + B \ln(DBH + 1)^2,$$ $$A = a + a_{ST} BA + a_{RDHP} \frac{DBH}{QMD} + a_{ALT} altitude + a_{PTOT} PTOT + a_{TMOY} TMOY + a_{SDOM} + a_{MP} + a_{VP} + a_{PERT},$$ where \(B\) is a species constant and every covariate effect interacts with \(\ln(DBH + 1)\). Height is not transformed, so no back-transformation applies. Grey birch (BETU.POP) has no \(\ln(DBH + 1)^2\) term in the source (Annexe 1) and is linear in \(\ln(DBH + 1)\).

Species-specific predictors (Tableau 5, pp. 10–11): BA is used for all species; the other predictors only for the species whose selected model contains them. A predictor is required only when a row's species uses it; otherwise it may be NULL or NA and is ignored. Use get_hd_model_info("auger2016") for definitions, and see the source for the per-species predictor sets. For example, white spruce (PICE.GLA) uses BA, QMD, TMOY, SDOM and VP; silver maple, American elm and grey birch use BA only.

Population-level prediction: the published fixed effects with the plot random effect and residual set to zero, i.e. the marginal prediction used by the source (p. 7). Plot calibration with measured heights is not implemented.

Class codes: classes with few observations were grouped by the author, and the group estimate is repeated for each member class (Annexes 2–4). A class with no estimate for a species (absent from its fitting data, e.g. physical environment 7 for red oak) gives an NA height and one warning per call. Codes are matched case-insensitively.

Coefficient precision: coefficients are used as printed (4 decimals). The altitude and precipitation slopes therefore carry about one significant digit; rounding can shift predictions by up to about 0.15 m.

Applicability: fitted to merchantable trees (DBH \(\ge\) 9.1 cm) of the Québec permanent and temporary inventory plots. The author advises against use for trees with DBH < 9 cm (p. 19); such trees are computed but reported as outside the range, and their predicted height may be below 1.3 m. Inputs outside the per-species ranges of the fitting data (Tableau 1: DBH and relative DBH; Tableau 2: BA, altitude, TMOY, PTOT) are computed and reported in a single warning. Rows with NA in a used input return NA height.

External implementation: the generalhdrelation2014 module of CFSForestTools reproduces the published coefficients for 10 species (PRUN.SER, ACER.SAC, FRAX.AME, FRAX.NIG, LARI.LAR, ULMU.AME, OSTR.VIR, PINU.STR, PINU.RES, TILI.AME; within 0.02 m) but uses different parameter estimates and predictor sets for the other 17 species (differences up to about 2.6 m). This function follows the publication.

References

Auger, I. (2016). Une nouvelle relation hauteur-diamètre tenant compte de l'influence de la station et du climat pour 27 essences commerciales du Québec. Gouvernement du Québec, ministère des Forêts, de la Faune et des Parcs, Direction de la recherche forestière. Note de recherche forestière no 146. 31 p.

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# Worked example (Annexe 1): white spruce, 12.0 m
hd_auger2016(
  DBH = 20, species = "PICE.GLA", BA = 20, QMD = 15,
  SDOM = "1", VP = "FC1", TMOY = 2.3
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   12.0

# Species needing only basal area
hd_auger2016(DBH = c(15, 30), species = c("ACER.SAC", "ULMU.AME"), BA = 25)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   15.8
#> 2   20.4

# Inside dplyr::mutate(): supply every predictor used by the species present
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(14, 22, 18),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "ABIE.BAL", "ACER.SAH"),
  BA = 22, QMD = c(15, 15, 20),
  SDOM = c("5ouest", "5ouest", "3ouest"), MP = c(2, 2, 2),
  VP = c("RS2", "RS2", "FE3"), TMOY = c(1, 1, 3.5),
  PTOT = 1000, altitude = 300, disturbance = "none"
)
dplyr::mutate(
  trees,
  hd_auger2016(DBH, species, BA, QMD, SDOM, MP, VP, TMOY, PTOT, altitude, disturbance)
)
#>   DBH  species BA QMD   SDOM MP  VP TMOY PTOT altitude disturbance   height
#> 1  14 PICE.MAR 22  15 5ouest  2 RS2  1.0 1000      300        none 12.30616
#> 2  22 ABIE.BAL 22  15 5ouest  2 RS2  1.0 1000      300        none 16.15196
#> 3  18 ACER.SAH 22  20 3ouest  2 FE3  3.5 1000      300        none 16.46363
